issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (Europe)

plan.diagnosis: Summit Continental Components S.p.A. (Italy) represents USD 1,115,982 in annual spend with a single-source sub-tier dependency among its 5 sub-tier suppliers, creating supply chain vulnerability. Despite a moderate resiliency score of 70, the supplier experienced 1 disruption event in the past 12 months, confirming exposure risk in the European supply base.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct sub-tier mapping workshop with Summit Continental to identify the single-source sub-tier supplier, document capabilities, lead times, and criticality to our bill of materials
Issue RFI to 3-5 qualified European sub-tier component manufacturers to assess technical capability, capacity, and willingness to serve as alternate source
Execute technical qualification and sample validation for top 2 alternate sub-tier candidates in collaboration with Summit Continental and Engineering
Negotiate dual-source agreement with Summit Continental requiring minimum 30% allocation to qualified alternate sub-tier supplier
Implement quarterly sub-tier risk reviews and update resiliency scoring in supplier performance management system

plan.expected_impact: Mitigating single-source sub-tier risk protects USD 1,115,982 in annual spend from potential disruption and is expected to reduce supply chain vulnerability costs by 15-20% (approximately USD 167,000-223,000 annually).
kpis: Sub-tier dual-source implementation rate (target: 100% by week 16)
Resiliency score improvement (target: 70 to 85+ within 6 months)
Disruption event frequency (target: reduce from 1 to 0 events over next 12 months)
Alternate sub-tier supplier qualification completion (target: 2 qualified sources)
Supply continuity risk exposure (target: reduce USD 1,115,982 single-source exposure by 70%)
risks: Summit Continental may resist sub-tier transparency or dual-sourcing due to margin pressure or proprietary relationships
Alternate sub-tier qualification may exceed 8-week timeline if technical requirements are complex or samples fail validation
Cost increase of 3-8% possible if alternate sub-tier supplier pricing is less competitive than incumbent
Short-term supply disruption risk during transition period if primary sub-tier performance degrades
Additional disruption events in Europe (geo_risk_region) could accelerate timeline pressure before alternates are qualified
erp_actions: SAP: Update LFA1/LFM1 supplier master for Summit Continental (IT) with sub-tier risk flag and mandatory dual-source requirement in purchasing info records
SAP: Create source list (ME01) entries for Summit Continental with quota arrangement (MEQ1) requiring 70/30 split once alternate sub-tier is qualified
Coupa: Add supplier risk attribute 'Single-Source Sub-Tier' and attach sub-tier mapping documentation to Summit Continental supplier record
Oracle EBS/Dynamics 365/NetSuite: Update supplier notes field with sub-tier risk status and link to approved alternate sub-tier list once qualified
SAP: Configure workflow (SWU3) to require Supplier Risk Manager approval for POs exceeding USD 50,000 to Summit Continental until dual-source implementation confirmed
All ERPs: Update payment terms to Net 45 (from standard Net 30) to improve working capital position during transition period, effective upon dual-source agreement execution
